4.A. History and Development of the Company
Corporate Structure
Our Company was incorporated in the Cayman Islands
on June 1, 2023, under the Companies Act as an exempted company with limited liability.
On October 3, 2023, the Company’s shareholders
and board of directors approved to amend the authorized share capital from US$50,000, divided into 50,000,000 ordinary shares of a par
value of US$0.001 per share, to US$50,000, divided into 500,000,000 ordinary shares of a par value of US$0.0001 per share. As of the date
of this annual report, there are 15,482,750 Ordinary Shares issued and outstanding.
Organization Chart
The chart below sets out our corporate structure.
Subsidiaries
A description of our subsidiaries are set out
below.
RPL
On December 26, 1997, RPL was incorporated in
Singapore as a private company limited by shares. It commenced business on December 26, 1997 and is engaged in the provision of industry
safety solutions to customers in the infrastructure, building construction, marine, and oil and gas industries. The products RPL provides
include (i) personal protective equipment, (ii) personal fall arrest systems, (iii) firefighting equipment and (iv) industrial graded
hardware.
As part of the Reorganization undertaken pursuant
to the Share Swap Agreement as described below, 3,000,000 ordinary shares, representing 100% of the equity in RPL, were transferred to
the Company, and RPL became a wholly owned subsidiary of our Company on January 3, 2024.
PTH
On November 3, 2008, PTH was incorporated in Singapore
as a private company limited by shares. It commenced business on November 3, 2008 and is engaged in the wholesale of general hardware,
including safety equipment, locks, hinges, and furniture. PTH is also engaged in providing electrical works for its customers.
As part of the Reorganization undertaken pursuant
to the Share Swap Agreement, 200,000 ordinary shares, representing 100% of the equity in PTH, were transferred to the Company, and PTH
became a wholly owned subsidiary of our Company on January 3, 2024.
ALS
On September 15, 2009, ALS was incorporated in
Singapore as a private company limited by shares. It commenced business on September 15, 2009 and is engaged in retail and wholesale of
general hardware.
As part of the Reorganization undertaken pursuant
to the Share Swap Agreement, 100,000 ordinary shares, representing 100% of the equity in ALS, were transferred to the Company, and ALS
became a wholly owned subsidiary of our Company on January 3, 2024.
Recent Developments
On September 8, 2025, the Company announced that
it had entered into a Standby Equity Purchase Agreement with Constantinople Limited and Chen Zhiqiang, pursuant to which the Company may,
at its discretion and subject to the satisfaction of applicable conditions, issue up to US$32,625,000 of ordinary shares to the investors
during the applicable commitment period. The purchase price for shares sold under the arrangement would be based on a 2.5% discount to
the lowest daily volume-weighted average price during the three consecutive trading days beginning on the trading day on which the Company
delivers an advance notice. The Company stated that it intended to use most of the proceeds from any sales under the agreement to purchase
Bitcoin, with the remainder to be used for general corporate purposes. We believe this filing is material because it represents both a
potential equity financing arrangement and a shift in treasury strategy. While the arrangement provides the Company with flexibility because
there are no mandatory minimum drawdowns and the Company controls the timing and size of advances, the proposed use of proceeds introduces
exposure to Bitcoin price volatility and digital asset treasury risks that differ meaningfully from the Company’s core business
of safety equipment, industrial products and clean-energy solutions. The Standby Equity Purchase Agreement was terminated on October 9,
2025.
On October 3, 2025, the Company announced that
Mr. Chan Yong Xian resigned as Chief Financial Officer of the Company, effective September 30, 2025. The Company stated that Mr. Chan’s
resignation was for personal reasons and was not due to any disagreement with the Company. To fill the vacancy, the Board appointed Mr.
Chan Kah Chun, then finance manager of the Company, as interim Chief Financial Officer effective October 1, 2025. Mr. Chan Kah Chun has
been with the Company for more than 10 years and has approximately 12 years of financial and accounting experience, including experience
in bank reconciliations, petty cash, inventory valuation, sales reporting and cash flow management. We believe this transition is important
from a governance and disclosure perspective because it involves a change in the Company’s principal financial officer. However,
the appointment of an internal finance executive with long tenure at the Company may provide continuity in the Company’s finance
function during the interim period. The Company also disclosed that Mr. Chan Kah Chun is not a member of the Board, has no family relationships
with any director or executive officer, and has no reportable related-party transactions with the Company.
On March 10, 2026, the Company announced that
it had adopted the Rectitude Holdings Ltd 2026 Equity Incentive Plan on March 4, 2026. The plan reserves up to 1,450,000 ordinary shares,
par value US$0.0001 per share, for issuance pursuant to awards granted under the plan. The Company stated that the purpose of the plan
is to motivate, attract and retain directors, consultants and key employees, encourage them to exert their best efforts on behalf of the
Company, and link their personal interests to those of the Company’s shareholders. We believe adoption of the plan is significant
because it provides the Company with a formal equity compensation framework following its Nasdaq listing, which may assist the Company
in recruiting and retaining talent as it expands its business lines, including industrial safety products and green-energy storage solutions.
At the same time, issuances under the plan may result in shareholder dilution, and the Company will need to administer awards in accordance
with applicable Nasdaq, SEC and corporate governance requirements.

4.B. Business Overview
Overview
Our business is principally involved in the provision
of safety equipment, encompassing essential items such as (i) personal protective clothing, hand gloves, safety footwear, and personal
fall arrest systems (a system used to arrest an employee in a fall from a walking-working surface, usually consisting of a body harness,
anchorage, and connector), (ii) portable fire extinguishers and (iii) traffic products such as rubber speed humps, wheel stops and wheel
chocks. Additionally, when needed by our customers, we also offer auxiliary products such as industrial hardware tools and electrical
hardware required for construction sites. For the financial years ended March 31, 2025 and March 31, 2024, the provision of safety equipment
contributed to 70.0% and 68.9% of our revenue, respectively. For the financial year ended March 31, 2026, we consolidated the revenue
for safety equipment and hardware products sale revenue as one group which is 98.0% of the total revenue.
Our products and solutions are marketed to a wide
array of distributor networks and end markets, both in Singapore and increasingly throughout the Southeast Asian region including Brunei,
Cambodia, Malaysia, Indonesia and Vietnam. The bulk of our customers belong to the infrastructure development, building construction,
marine, oil and gas industries, and general industrial markets. This broad market coverage allows us to serve a diverse customer base
and capitalize on growth opportunities in various sectors. Our business strategy involves enhancing our market presence in Singapore and
increasingly, the Southeast Asian region as well as executing selected acquisitions that meet our specific investment criteria.
